transcript.text: theres a funny smell from my oven when its on

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. A funny smell when an oven is first used can be normal. If it’s a new oven (or one you’ve just deep-cleaned), the smell is likely from the protective coating on the elements burning off or food residue charring; this should fade after a few hours of use at high heat. However, if the smell resembles burning plastic, insulation, or smoke, or if it persists, it could indicate an electrical fault such as a loose mains connection or a failing heating element. Because these can be fire hazards, please stop using the oven immediately if you suspect an electrical issue and have it checked by a qualified engineer. To help narrow this down: is the oven brand new (or recently cleaned), and does the smell resemble burning plastic/electrical insulation or just a temporary 'new appliance' odour?
its not new, about 12 years old and not cleaned recently. smells more like hot plastic or electrical, seems to come from behind or underneath rather than inside the oven

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Given the age (12 years) and that the smell is coming from behind or underneath, this points strongly to an electrical fault inside the chassis rather than just food residue burning off. The most likely cause is the mains terminal block where the power cable enters the oven has become loose or overheated over time, melting nearby insulation. This is a serious fire risk. Please do not use the oven again until it has been inspected by a qualified engineer. They will need to isolate the appliance at the fuse box and open up the rear panel to check for burnt connections or damaged wiring.
